gate.text: Only someone with access to the server can start setup. Enter the token printed by the installer, or generate a new one on the server with:
gate.tokenHelp: Valid for 1 hour. The browser keeps it only in a secure cookie.
gate.adminExists: An administrator account exists. Sign in as an administrator to continue setup.

language.title: Language
language.help: Default language for setup and the administrator account. You can change it in the panel at any time.

checks.title: System pre-checks
checks.help: Checks the API can verify from its own container: PostgreSQL, Redis, database migrations and the background worker. Operating system, disk and port checks run on the server with "sh scripts/install.sh check".

access.title: Deployment and access address
access.help: The address users will open the panel at. The test checks whether the server can reach itself through this address. Behind NAT a server may not reach its own public address; then the address is saved as unverified.

domain.title: Domain and HTTPS
domain.help: The name the panel will be opened at over HTTPS from the internet. DNS, HTTP reachability and the certificate are tested separately; one passing does not mean the others pass. You can also run without a domain: skip this step and use 127.0.0.1 or an SSH tunnel.

services.title: PostgreSQL and Redis
services.help: The application's database and queue connections. These services run only on the internal Docker network and are never exposed to the internet.

admin.title: Administrator account
admin.help: The first account that manages the panel. After this step the setup token stops working and setup continues only with this account.

vmware.title: ESXi / vCenter connection
vmware.help: The VMware infrastructure the platform will manage virtual servers on. Add a standalone ESXi or a vCenter. vCenter does not replace ESXi; it manages hosts centrally. Do not also add a vCenter-managed host as a standalone ESXi.

discovery.title: Datastore and network discovery
discovery.help: The real hosts, datastores, networks and virtual machines read from the connections.

pools.title: Resource pool and IP plan
pools.help: Capacity and IP ranges to offer for sale or use.

monitoring.title: Monitoring and notifications
monitoring.help: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Alertmanager are optional and run in a separate Compose profile. To receive alerts, add a webhook or e-mail receiver to data/observability/alertmanager.yml on the server.

summary.title: Final check and summary
summary.help: Status of each step. Setup cannot finish until required steps are done. Once finished, setup endpoints close; reopening needs "node dist/cli.js recover-setup" on the server.

notAvailable.pools: Resource pools are created in Admin → Catalog; this wizard step comes later.

access.label: Panel address
access.help: Examples: https://panel.example.com or http://127.0.0.1:8080 through an SSH tunnel. Do not add a path, query or user info.

hint.DNS_FAILED: The domain did not resolve. Check that the A record points to the server's public IP and has propagated.
hint.CONNECTION_REFUSED: Connection refused. Check port forwarding, the firewall and the address Caddy listens on (LISTEN_ADDRESS).
hint.TIMEOUT: Timed out. A firewall or NAT may be dropping the connection.
hint.TLS_ERROR: The TLS certificate could not be verified. Do not disable certificate checks; fix the certificate and domain.
hint.WRONG_TARGET: This address answers but is not this installation. DNS or a proxy points to another server.
hint.HTTP_ERROR: The address returned an unexpected HTTP response. A proxy in front may not forward /api to this installation.
hint.LOOPBACK_NOT_VERIFIABLE: 127.0.0.1 and localhost cannot be verified from inside the container. You can save it for use through an SSH tunnel.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The address could not be reached. Check the address and the network path.

admin.done: The administrator account has been created.

monitoring.enable: I will use the monitoring components
monitoring.help: First start the monitoring profile on the server, then test the connection:

summary.warnVmware: No VMware connection configured: the platform cannot create or manage virtual servers yet.
summary.warnAccess: The panel address could not be verified from this server. Open it from another device to check.
summary.warnHttps: HTTPS is not configured. Do not expose the panel to the internet; use 127.0.0.1 or an SSH tunnel, or complete the domain step.

checkCodes.NO_HEARTBEAT: No signal in the last 90 seconds
checkCodes.TLS_ERROR: TLS certificate could not be verified
checkCodes.CERT_STAGING: Let's Encrypt test (staging) certificate; browsers do not trust it

domain.label: Domain name
domain.help: Example: panel.example.com. A subdomain is recommended rather than the bare domain.

howto.dnsRecord: At your DNS provider create an A record for this name pointing to the server's public IPv4 address. Add an AAAA record only if the server has working public IPv6. Do not enter a private address (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x); behind NAT enter your router's public address and forward ports 80/443 to this server.
howto.ports: Ports 80 and 443 must reach this server from the internet: Let's Encrypt validates over 80 (HTTP-01) or 443 (TLS-ALPN-01). If another web server uses these ports, use the 'behind-proxy' mode.
howto.apply: Run the command below on the server. Use --acme-staging first while testing so repeated attempts do not hit real certificate rate limits. Once it works, run it again without that option.
howto.test: Then use 'Test connection' to check DNS, HTTP and the certificate separately. Caddy renews the certificate automatically and keeps it in a persistent volume (caddy_data).

domain.behindProxy: To run behind an existing Nginx/Caddy/Traefik use 'sudo sh scripts/install.sh behind-proxy': the panel listens with plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 and your proxy terminates TLS. Details: docs/domain-https.md
domain.aaaaWarning: This name has an AAAA (IPv6) record. If IPv6 does not really work on the server, remove the record; otherwise some visitors and certificate validation will fail.

hint.DNS_FAILED: The name did not resolve. Create the A record and wait for it to propagate (minutes to hours).
hint.NO_ADDRESS_RECORDS: The name exists but has no A record. Add an A record pointing to the server's public IPv4 address.
hint.CONNECTION_REFUSED: Connection refused: nothing listens on that port. Did you run the installer's 'domain' command? A firewall or port forwarding may block 80/443.
hint.TIMEOUT: Timed out: a firewall or NAT may be dropping the connection. Open 80/443 in your cloud provider's firewall.
hint.HTTP_ERROR: Unexpected HTTP response. A proxy or CDN in front may not forward requests to this installation.
hint.TLS_ERROR: The certificate could not be verified (expired, for another name or self-signed). Do not disable certificate checks; check the domain and Caddy logs: docker compose logs proxy
hint.CERT_STAGING: This is a test certificate. If everything works, run the command again without --acme-staging to get a real certificate.
hint.WRONG_TARGET: This name answers but is not this installation. DNS or a proxy in front points to another server.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The address could not be reached.

vmware.note: The step completes once a connection is added. The detailed inventory is on the VMware page of the admin panel. If you skip this step the platform cannot manage virtual servers.

discovery.none: No connections yet. Go back a step or skip this one.

Vmware.title: ESXi and vCenter connections
Vmware.intro: Real inventory and physical capacity. The platform changes nothing here; it only reads.
Vmware.testOk: Connection succeeded: {kind}. Found {hosts} hosts and {vms} virtual machines. Not saved yet.

form.name: Display name
form.nameHelp: Name shown in the panel, for example 'Frankfurt vCenter'.
form.hostHelp: Management name or IP of the ESXi or vCenter. It must be reachable from the platform server; your browser does not need to reach it.
form.usernameHelp: A dedicated account with the needed privileges is recommended (vCenter example: lightning@vsphere.local).
form.passwordHelp: Stored encrypted; never sent back to the browser and never logged.
form.tlsHelp: Verification is never turned off in any mode.
form.caPemHelp: The vCenter VMCA root certificate or your organisation's CA.
form.sha256Help: Only this exact certificate is accepted. Update it when the certificate is renewed.
form.groupEndpointHelp: The name or IP address of vCenter or ESXi, as the panel reaches it.
form.groupAccountHelp: The account the panel uses. A separate account with only the needed privileges is recommended.

cert.title: Presented certificate
cert.explain: This certificate is not trusted yet. Verify the fingerprint on the server itself before connecting.
cert.subject: Subject
cert.pin: I verified the fingerprint, pin this certificate

writeApiNote.restricted: The license looks like the free vSphere Hypervisor: the VMware API is read-only. Server creation and power actions are not possible through this connection.
writeApiNote.unknown: The license could not be read; whether write operations work must be confirmed with a real operation.

warning.HOST_MANAGED_BY_VCENTER: This ESXi is managed by a vCenter. Add the vCenter instead of the host.
warning.LICENSE_UNREADABLE: License information could not be read.
warning.PRIVILEGES_UNREADABLE: The service account's privileges could not be read; operations show as unavailable.
warning.VERSION_LEGACY: This vSphere version (before 7.0) is out of vendor support and not officially supported by our library. Basic operations work; it receives no security updates.
warning.VERSION_END_OF_SUPPORT: General support for this vSphere version has ended (6.7 and 7.0). It keeps working; upgrading to 8.0 or later is recommended.
warning.CUSTOMIZATION_GUESTINFO: Before vCenter 7.0 U3 there is no native cloud-init customization. New servers get their cloud-init data through guestinfo; the template needs cloud-init 21.3+ with the VMware datasource.
warning.FEDERATED_LOGIN_BLOCKED: vCenter 9 blocks password sign-in for identity-federated accounts. Use a vsphere.local or LDAP/AD service account for this connection.

Vmware.capacityNote: Real values of the hosts and datastores. Headroom, capacity offered for sale and reserved capacity are shown per resource pool in Admin → Catalog.

remove.title: Remove connection
remove.explain: Removed only from this panel: the ESXi/vCenter and its virtual machines are not touched. The stored password and inventory are deleted.

compat.title: Version compatibility
compat.intro: The detected vSphere version and the methods used with it. You can pin an older API version or choose the customization method if needed.
compat.formHelp: “Detect automatically” is right in most cases. A manual choice can only go below the detected version.
compat.versionHelp: Automatic: the version the server reports is used (6.0 – 9.x).
compat.customizationHelp: How new servers get their network, name and SSH keys.

methodHelp.auto: The best method for the version is chosen.
methodHelp.guestinfo: Works on every version; needs cloud-init 21.3+ in the template.

compat.saved: Saved; the connection was re-discovered with the new setting.

Console.title: Console: {name}
Console.osLogin: The console connects to the virtual machine's screen; it does not bypass the operating system's login. A user name and password are still needed.
Console.sdkMissing: The VMware HTML Console SDK is not installed. Its license terms keep it out of this project; download it from Broadcom's developer portal and put these files into the console-sdk/ folder on the server (docs/console.md):

state.error: The console could not be opened

probe.ok: Success: the gateway reached the VM's console endpoint and received data (network path, certificate pinning and ticket work).

reason.CONSOLE_SESSION_INVALID: The console session is invalid, expired or already used. Open the console again.
reason.CONSOLE_REVOKED: The console was closed: the session ended or access was withdrawn.
reason.CONSOLE_EXPIRED: The console reached its maximum duration and was closed. You can open it again.
reason.CONSOLE_LIMIT: The limit of simultaneous consoles was reached. Close another console.
reason.CONSOLE_UNREACHABLE: The console gateway could not reach the VM's host (network access). Check that the panel server can reach the ESXi management network.
reason.CONSOLE_TLS_MISMATCH: The host's certificate did not match the thumbprint VMware reported; the connection was not made, for safety.
reason.CONSOLE_TICKET_REJECTED: The host rejected the console ticket. Open the console again.
reason.CONSOLE_ENDPOINT_BLOCKED: Connecting to the console address VMware returned is not allowed (local or internal network).

Catalog.title: Resource pools and catalog
Catalog.intro: Open existing VMware capacity for sale or use; manage packages, rules, images, IP pools and quotas.
Catalog.poolsExplain: A resource pool creates no physical resources; it opens part of the existing infrastructure's capacity for sale or use. Physical total, management/safety headroom, offered, reserved and really used capacity are shown separately.

warning.STORAGE_FREE_BELOW_HEADROOM: Real free space on the datastores is below the safety headroom.
warning.STORAGE_OVERPROVISIONED: Thin disks promise more than the physical capacity; space may run out as disks fill.
warning.MEMORY_OVERCOMMITTED: RAM assigned to existing VMs exceeds physical RAM.

pools.title: Resource pools
pools.storageNote: Storage: {written} GB written, {provisioned} GB provisioned (thin), real free space {free} GB.
pools.locationHelp: Location name shown to customers (example: Frankfurt).
pools.memoryOvercommitHelp: 1 is recommended; RAM overcommit causes performance problems (1–4).
pools.storageOvercommitHelp: How many times the capacity may be offered with thin disks (1–10).
pools.reserveCpuPctHelp: Management and safety headroom that is never offered.
pools.reserveMemoryPctHelp: Management and safety headroom that is never offered.
pools.reserveStoragePctHelp: Never offered; you are warned when real free space falls below it.

rule.explain: Ranges, steps, allowed RAM per vCPU and unit prices (monthly) customers can choose in this pool.

images.title: Operating system images
images.explain: Images are VM templates in a connection's inventory. The template is prepared in VMware; the platform only selects it here.
images.noTemplates: No templates found in this connection.

ip.title: IP pools
ip.explain: IPv4 only for now. Ranges cannot overlap within one resource pool. Addresses are assigned automatically when a server is created and released after it is deleted.

quotas.title: Quotas
quotas.explain: The default quota applies to everyone; a user quota replaces the default. An empty field is unlimited.

form.poolIdentityHelp: The location name customers see when ordering.
form.vmwareHelp: The cluster/host, network and datastores this pool's servers are created on.
form.datastoresHelp: With several, the one with most free space is used.
form.overcommitHelp: How many virtual units are sold per physical one. 4 is common for CPU; 1 is safe for memory.
form.reserveHelp: The part of physical capacity kept off sale for management and load spikes.
form.pricingHelp: Monthly unit prices; the total is computed from them.
form.imageIdentityHelp: The operating system name customers pick when ordering.
form.templateHelp: Pick a template with cloud-init. Only machines marked as templates are listed.
form.minDiskHelp: This image cannot be installed on a smaller disk; smaller packages do not offer it.
form.resourcesHelp: The virtual hardware the server gets.
form.hourlyHelp: Leave empty to use the monthly price / 730.
form.whereHelp: The locations the package is sold in and the operating systems it can run.
form.diskTooSmall: The disk is too small for: {images}.
form.networkHelp: Subnet and gateway. Typing a CIDR suggests the gateway and range.
form.rangeHelp: Servers get addresses from this range in order. Excluded ones are skipped.
form.scopeHelp: The default applies to everyone; pick a user to set theirs.

ipm.extraTitle: Extra IPv4 for sale (up to {n} per server)
ipm.extraPriceHelp: In the currency of the package or custom offer
ipm.quarantineHelp: A deleted server’s addresses wait this long before another customer gets them (their reputation may still be the previous customer’s). 0 = no quarantine.
ipm.ipv6Help: Optional: a /48–/64 prefix routed to the same network. Every new server gets one IPv6 address from it, configured automatically.
ipm.excludedHelp: Never handed out (routers, your own machines, reserved for customers)
ipm.addressesHelp: Every address that is not simply free: in use (with the server, its owner and reverse DNS), in quarantine, or excluded.

step.readiness: waiting for the operating system to be ready

confirm.power_off: Force off cuts power without telling the operating system; unsaved data may be lost.
confirm.reset: Reset restarts without telling the operating system; unsaved data may be lost.

Servers.powerExplain: Shut down asks the operating system to stop (needs VMware Tools). Force off and reset do not.
Servers.readinessExplain: "Ready": the VM is on, VMware Tools runs and the operating system reports the assigned IP address. A powered-on VM alone is not ready.
Servers.metricsEmpty: No metrics are collected for this server yet. No sample or estimated values are shown.

delete.title: Delete server
delete.explain: The VM is deleted in VMware. The IP address and reserved capacity are released only after VMware confirms the VM is gone. This cannot be undone.

keys.title: SSH keys
keys.explain: Public keys are installed on the server with cloud-init. SSH password login is created disabled.
keys.name: Key name

admin.title: Servers and operations
admin.intro: All servers, automation jobs, failed operations and reconciliation with VMware.
admin.reconcileExplain: Compares the platform's records with the real state in VMware. It reports findings; it never deletes anything by itself.
admin.search: Search by name, owner, IP or pool

ips.title: IP addresses
ips.help: Reverse DNS (PTR) can be set for each address.
ips.helpForward: Reverse DNS (PTR) can be set for each address. The name must resolve to the address first (A or AAAA record).
ips.helpLocked: Reverse DNS is managed by your provider.

Maintenance.title: Backups and updates
Maintenance.settings: Scheduled maintenance: {schedule} · keep {keep} local backups · external copy: {copy} · automatic update: {auto} (channel {channel}, window {window})
Maintenance.explain: Backups, restores and updates run on the server with scripts/install.sh (backup, restore, update, schedule, auto-update). The panel only shows their results. Backups hold the panel's own data, not customer VMs; a VMware snapshot is not a backup.

code.E_BACKUP_KEY_MISSING: the backup key secrets/backup.key is missing
code.E_BACKUP_DB: the database could not be dumped
code.E_BACKUP_VERIFY: the backup file could not be read back (disk full?)
code.E_BACKUP_COPY: written locally but not copied to the external target
code.E_RESTORE_DB: the database could not be restored
code.E_RESTORE_START: data restored but the services did not become ready
code.E_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE: that version lacks a migration already applied (no database downgrade)
code.E_UPDATE_FAILED: the new version did not become ready
code.W_UPDATE_BUSY: operations were running; tried again in the next hour

Dashboard.title: Overview
Dashboard.intro: Servers, sellable capacity, operations and connections at a glance.
Dashboard.setupIncomplete: Initial setup is not finished yet.
Dashboard.gettingStartedHelp: Complete these steps before customers can create servers.

stat.failed: {n, plural, =0 {0 failed in 24 h} one {# failed in 24 h} other {# failed in 24 h}}

chart.capacityHelp: Used by other VMs, reserved by Lightning VM servers, still sellable.

security.title: Sign-in and security

security.passkeysHelp: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or security key instead of a password. Passkeys belong to this panel's address.
security.passkeysNeedHttps: Passkeys need HTTPS (or localhost). Open the panel over its HTTPS address to add one.

profile.title: Profile
profile.intro: The name shown in the panel.
profile.name: Full name
profile.emailHelp: This is your sign-in name; ask an administrator to change it.

twoFactor.sectionIntro: Besides your password: an authenticator app, or a code by SMS or e-mail.
twoFactor.title: Authenticator app
twoFactor.intro: 6-digit codes from an app such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password.
twoFactor.scan1: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
twoFactor.scan2: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows.
twoFactor.manual: If you cannot scan, enter this key:
twoFactor.backupHelp: Use these to sign in if you lose your phone. Each works once; keep them somewhere safe. They are not shown again.

phone.title: Phone number
phone.intro: A verified number can receive sign-in codes and notifications by SMS.
phone.unavailable: SMS is not set up yet; once your administrator adds an SMS provider you can verify a number.
phone.help: With the country code. Numbers starting with 05xx are completed as +90.

SERVER_OFF_LONG.body: If you do not use it, delete it to free its resources.

ENABLE_2FA.body: It protects your account against leaked passwords.

Metrics.noSamples: No samples yet; they appear within a few minutes.

Notify.title: Notification preferences
Notify.intro: Choose how each notification reaches you. The choices are limited to the channels your administrator allows.
Notify.none: No notifications can be sent to you.
Notify.channelsIntro: The ways notifications can reach you, and their status. Test each one here.

channelHelp.inApp: Shown under the bell, top right.
channelHelp.push: A system notification on this device, even when the panel is closed.
channelHelp.sms: Sent to your verified phone number.

unavailable.push: This browser does not support it.
unavailable.email: Outgoing mail is not set up.

Notify.needPhone: Verify your phone number on the Security tab first.
Notify.needPush: Turn on browser notifications on this device first.
Notify.pushDenied: The browser refused notifications. You can allow them in the site settings.
Notify.pushUnsupported: This browser does not support Web Push.
Notify.lockedHelp: Your administrator fixed this notification; it cannot be changed.
Notify.notOffered: This channel is not offered for this notification
Notify.policyNote: Locked notifications and channels not offered come from your administrator's notification rules.

server_ready.title: Server ready
server_ready.help: When your new server is set up and running.

server_failed.title: Server operation failed
server_failed.help: When a create, power or delete operation fails.

server_deleted.title: Server deleted
server_deleted.help: When a server and its disks were removed.

server_power.title: Power operation done

auth_sign_in.help: When someone signs in to your account.

auth_two_factor_changed.title: Two-factor changed
auth_two_factor_changed.help: When it is turned on or off.

admin_operation_failed.help: When any customer's operation fails for good.

server_firewall_failed.title: Firewall not applied
server_firewall_failed.help: When the rules of a firewall could not be written to a server.

Notify.policyTitle: The admin first, then each user
Notify.policyIntro: For each notification, choose which channels may be used, which are on by default, and whether users may change it. Users can only choose among what you allow here.

audienceHelp.user: Sent to each user about their own account and servers.
audienceHelp.staff: Sent to team members with the matching permission.

Users.title: Users
Users.intro: Accounts, roles, personal permissions, sessions and security status.
Users.search: Search by e-mail, name or phone

form.name: Full name
form.passwordHelp: A strong password was generated; give it to the user securely.
form.rolesHelp: Several roles can be chosen; their permissions add up.
form.copiedOnSave: Copied to the clipboard when saved.

Users.rolesExplain: Roles' permissions add up. You cannot give a permission you do not have.
Users.adminHasAll: The administrator role has every permission; no personal permissions are needed.
Users.overridesHelp: Click a permission: it removes one that comes from a role, or adds one the roles lack. Click again to undo.
Users.banExplain: A banned user cannot sign in; their sessions and consoles close at once. Their servers are not deleted.
Users.banReasonHelp: Written to the audit log and the user list.
Users.passwordSet: Password changed and copied to the clipboard.
Users.passwordExplain: The user's current password changes. Give the new one to them securely.
Users.hasServers: This user has {n} servers. Delete them first.
Users.removeExplain: The account, sessions, passkeys and SSH keys are removed for good. This cannot be undone.

Roles.title: Roles
Roles.intro: A role is a named set of permissions. Users get one or more roles on the Users page; single permissions can also be added or removed per user.
Roles.removeBody: Its {n} members keep their other roles; anyone left without one becomes “Customer”.
Roles.name: Name
Roles.keyHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _; cannot be changed later.

desc.user: Orders and manages their own servers.
desc.operator: Runs the infrastructure: all servers, operations, VMware and capacity.
desc.support: Helps customers: sees users and servers, can sign in as a customer.
desc.auditor: Sees everything read-only, including the audit log.

help.dashboard_view: The admin dashboard, insights and summary charts.
help.servers_create: Create new servers for their own account.
help.servers_view_all: See everyone's servers, operations and reconciliation findings.
help.servers_manage_all: Power on, off, reset and delete other people's servers.
help.operations_retry: Resume a failed automation operation from its last step.
help.reconcile_run: Check the panel against VMware right away.
help.consoles_any: Open the browser console of any VM and close open consoles.
help.catalog_view: Pools, packages, images, IP pools and quotas (read only).
help.catalog_manage: Add, change and remove pools, packages, images, IP pools and quotas.
help.users_view: User list, roles, sessions and security status.
help.users_manage: Create users, change their details and password, remove them.
help.users_roles: Give users roles and personal permissions (only up to their own).
help.users_ban: Ban users for a while or for good, and lift bans.
help.users_impersonate: See a user's account as they do, for support (recorded).
help.roles_manage: Create roles, change their permissions, remove them.

help.settings_manage: Change those settings and test the integrations.
help.firewalls_manage: Create firewalls and attach them to their own servers.
help.system_update: Check for updates, update, back up and set automatic updates from the panel.

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.intro: Branding, e-mail, bot protection, SMS and notification rules. Every integration can be tested before you save it.
Settings.readOnly: You can see the settings but not change them.
Settings.secretHelp: Leave empty to keep the stored value.

branding.image_type: Choose a PNG, JPEG, WebP or ICO file.
branding.image_size: The file cannot be larger than 256 KB.
branding.image_read: The file could not be read.
branding.logoHelp: Square, at least 64×64 px PNG/WebP recommended; at most 256 KB.
branding.faviconHelp: 32×32 or 48×48 px PNG or ICO; at most 256 KB.
branding.identityHelp: Shown in the menu, on the sign-in page, in the tab title and in e-mails.
branding.name: Panel name
branding.colorHelp: Buttons, links and selected items use this colour. The text colour on it is picked for readability.
branding.lowContrast: This colour may be hard to read (light background {light}:1, dark background {dark}:1; at least 3:1 recommended).
branding.logoSection: Shown next to the name in the menu and on the sign-in page.
branding.faviconSection: The small icon in the browser tab and in notifications.

mail.serverHelp: The server the panel sends e-mail through. Pick a known provider and fill in the rest.
mail.envFallback: SMTP_URL from the install file (.env) is used now. Once you save here, these settings apply.
mail.presetHelp: Fills in server, port and security; you enter the username and password.
mail.insecure: Without encryption, the password and e-mails travel in plain text. Use only on a trusted internal network.
mail.authHelp: SMTP username and password. Gmail and Microsoft 365 need an app password.
mail.senderHelp: The name and address recipients see. The address must be verified with your SMTP provider.
mail.useHelp: E-mails that are part of a task. Which channel each notification uses is on the “Notification rules” tab.
mail.usePasswordResetHelp: “Forgot password” appears on the sign-in page.
mail.useTwoFactorHelp: Without SMS, sign-in codes are sent by e-mail.
mail.notificationsNote: For notification e-mails (server ready, new sign-in…), turn on the e-mail channel on the Notification rules tab.
mail.testHelp: Connects, signs in and sends one test e-mail with the values in the form (without saving).

captcha.providerHelp: Protects the sign-in, sign-up and password reset forms from bots. You get the keys from the provider.
captcha.envFallback: The Turnstile keys from the install file are used now. Once you save here, these settings apply.

d.recaptcha-v2: The “I am not a robot” checkbox.

captcha.keysHelp: The site key is used in the browser, the secret only on the server. Remember to add your domain at the provider.
captcha.minScoreHelp: Between 0 and 1; requests below are refused. 0.5 is a good start.
captcha.whereHelp: The chosen forms ask for the check before they are sent.
captcha.testHelp: Solve the check with the site key you entered, then have the provider verify it with the secret.
captcha.invisible: reCAPTCHA v3 is invisible; the test runs it in the background.
captcha.widgetFailed: The check could not load; verify the site key and the domain setting.

sms.providerHelp: The APIs of Turkish providers are built in; for any other service use “Custom HTTP API”.

confidenceHelp.partial: This provider's docs do not fully describe the response. Send a test before you save.
confidenceHelp.community: No public API docs were found for this provider; the integration follows other projects. Test it.

sms.accountHelp: The API details from the provider's panel. Secret fields are stored encrypted and never shown again.

fieldHelp.url: The {to}, {text} and {sender} placeholders are filled in.
fieldHelp.body: POST body; the same placeholders work.
fieldHelp.headers: A JSON object, for example with an Authorization key and value.
fieldHelp.successPattern: If the response matches this regular expression, the message counts as sent. Example: ^OK
fieldHelp.phoneFormat: The number format the provider expects.
fieldHelp.apiHash: In the panel under Settings > Security > API Access.
fieldHelp.operator: The operator your account belongs to.

sms.senderHelp: The header shown on messages. It must be approved at the provider.
sms.senderNumeric: This provider takes the numeric id of the header, not its name.
sms.senderLabelHelp: Up to 11 characters, exactly as registered at the provider.
sms.commercialHelp: Campaign-type messages go through the İYS check. Codes and notifications are informational; usually leave this off.
sms.useHelp: SMS that are part of a task. To send notifications by SMS, turn on the SMS channel on the Notification rules tab.
sms.useTwoFactorHelp: Users with a verified phone get sign-in codes by SMS.
sms.usePhoneHelp: Users verify their number with an SMS code on My account.
sms.notificationsNote: Notification SMS go only to users who verified their phone.
sms.testHelp: Sends one real SMS with the values in the form (without saving).

payments.activeHelp: Offered to customers in this order. Each one runs in the mode you chose (live or test).
payments.noneActive: No payment method is active. Pick a provider below, enter its credentials, check them and activate it.

confidence.community: from open-source integrations; confirm with the provider

payments.label: Name shown to customers
payments.labelHelp: Optional; the provider name is used otherwise.
payments.useModeHelp: Both credential sets are kept; this decides which one payments use.
payments.only3d: checked only by a real 3D Secure payment
payments.liveWarning: Live credentials take real payments. Enter the values from the provider’s production merchant panel.
payments.testHelp: Test (sandbox) credentials: payments here never move money. Use the provider’s test panel and test cards.
payments.fillTest: Fill in the public test account
payments.fillTestHelp: Published by the provider or its integrators; may change.
payments.endpointHelp: Leave empty to use the address shown. Only if the provider gave you a different one.
payments.checkHow: Sends a request that moves no money (a card BIN or installment query, a token request, or a status query for an order that does not exist) and reads the answer.
payments.checkNone: This provider has no request that can check credentials without starting a payment. Verify them with a test payment.

checkExplain.rejected: The provider refused them; see its message.
checkExplain.inconclusive: The provider answered, but not in a way that proves the credentials. Read its message.
checkExplain.network: Network, TLS or IP restriction problem. Many providers only accept registered server IPs.
checkExplain.unverifiable: No online check exists for this provider.

payments.unverified: Not verifiable by any API: {fields}. Confirm with a test 3D Secure payment.
payments.notRecorded: These values differ from the saved ones: save them, then check again to be able to activate.
payments.removeBody: Both credential sets and check results are deleted.

notes.NO_SANDBOX_HOST: There is no separate test server: test credentials use the live address.
notes.TEST_HOST_UNCERTAIN: Sources disagree about the test address. If the check cannot reach it, ask the provider and set it under Advanced.
notes.FIXED_IP: The provider only accepts requests from a registered fixed IP: register this server’s public IP in its panel.
notes.TOKEN_ROTATES: Each check issues a new access token, which ends the previous one. Avoid checking live credentials during live traffic.
notes.WALLET_ONLY: A wallet payment (the customer pays from their account), not a card virtual POS.
notes.NO_SERVER_CHECK: Credentials cannot be checked online for this provider; activation records that it was not verified.
notes.THREE_D_KEY: The 3D Secure key is used only in the bank’s 3D form; only a real test payment proves it.
notes.IP_WHITELIST: Banks usually require the server’s IP to be registered for live use.
notes.SAME_HOST_FOR_TEST: Test and live use the same address; test mode is chosen by the credentials or a test flag.

rdns.providerHelp: The PowerDNS server that holds the reverse zones (in-addr.arpa, ip6.arpa) of your IP blocks. The panel writes PTR records through its HTTP API.

providers.powerdns: Also PowerDNS-Admin setups: the panel talks to PowerDNS directly.

rdns.apiUrlHelp: The PowerDNS webserver, for example http://10.0.0.53:8081 (api=yes, webserver-allow-from must include this server)
rdns.ttlHelp: Seconds the records may be cached
rdns.defaultsHelp: New servers get this PTR on all their addresses. Deleting a server removes its records.
rdns.templateHelp: Variables: {ip}, {ipDashed}, {name}. Empty: new servers get no PTR.
rdns.customerEdit: Customers may change the PTR of their addresses
rdns.forwardCheck: Only names that resolve back to the address (forward-confirmed)
rdns.forwardHelp: The forward check stops customers from naming an address after a domain they do not control. Staff are not checked.
rdns.noZones: No reverse zones on this server. Create the zones of your blocks first (for example 113.0.203.in-addr.arpa).

Firewalls.title: Firewalls
Firewalls.intro: Rule sets you attach to your servers. Everything coming in that no rule allows is dropped; outgoing traffic is open unless you add outbound rules. VMware enforces the rules on the virtual switch, so they work whatever runs inside the server.
Firewalls.emptyBody: Create one from a template (for example a web server: SSH, HTTP, HTTPS and ping) and attach it to your servers.
Firewalls.name: Name
Firewalls.templateHelp: You can change every rule afterwards.

templateDesc.empty: No rules: nothing reaches the server until you add some.
templateDesc.web: SSH, HTTP, HTTPS and ping from anywhere.
templateDesc.windows: Remote Desktop and ping from anywhere.

Firewalls.applyHelp: A server can have up to {n} firewalls; their rules add up.
Firewalls.removeBody: The firewall and its rules are deleted.
Firewalls.removeInUse: It is still attached to {n, plural, one {# server} other {# servers}}. Detach it first.
Firewalls.howBody: Inbound: only what a rule allows gets in (replies to connections the server opens itself are always allowed). Outbound: everything is allowed until you add an outbound rule; then only what the rules allow goes out. Changes are applied to all attached servers within seconds.
Firewalls.inboundHelp: Traffic to your server. Sources: which addresses may connect.
Firewalls.outboundHelp: Traffic from your server. Leave empty to allow all outgoing traffic.
Firewalls.noInbound: No inbound rules: all incoming traffic is blocked.
Firewalls.noOutbound: No outbound rules: all outgoing traffic is allowed.
Firewalls.ipsHelp: addresses or networks, separated by commas
Firewalls.serversHelp: Servers protected by this firewall (at most {n} firewalls per server).
Firewalls.pendingHelp: means the new rules are being written to VMware.
Firewalls.serverOpen: No firewall: every port of this server is reachable.
Firewalls.serverNone: No firewall is attached. Attach one from the Firewalls page.
Firewalls.orderHelp: Optional. Applied before the server first starts.

Updates.title: Updates
Updates.intro: Check for new versions and update from here. The server runs the same update as the command line: a backup first, running tasks paused, the new version started and checked, and an automatic rollback if it does not come up.
Updates.agentMissingTitle: The update agent is not installed on this server
Updates.agentMissing: The panel cannot run anything on the host by itself. Install the agent once (new installs have it):

channelHelp.edge: Every change on the branch; for test servers.

Updates.availableHelp: Takes a few minutes. The panel restarts and may not answer for a short while.

confirm.step1: An encrypted backup is taken first; nothing changes if it fails.
confirm.step2: Running server tasks are paused and continue afterwards from their last step.
confirm.step3: The new version is built and started; the panel is unavailable for a few minutes.
confirm.step4: If it does not become ready, the previous version is started again automatically.
confirm.step5: Database changes are not undone automatically; the backup can restore them.

Updates.restarting: The panel is restarting with the new version. This page keeps trying and continues on its own.
Updates.failed: The task failed ({code}). The log below says why; with a failed update the previous version is running again.
Updates.switchHelp: Moves to this version with the same safety steps. Going back to an older version is refused when the database was already changed by a newer one.
